relationships.subject: paclitaxel
relationships.evidence_quote: Taken together, these results indicate that paclitaxel treatment increases m6A abundance and METTL14 expression in rat and human DRG.

relationships.subject: METTL14
relationships.evidence_quote: Collectively, our results suggest that METTL14 mediates paclitaxel-induced m6A upregulation in the DRG.

relationships.subject: METTL14
relationships.evidence_quote: Conversely, AAV9-mediated Mettl14 overexpression markedly increased the expression of Grin2a and Grin2b, but not Grin1, in the DRG, with Grin2a exhibiting the most dramatic change

relationships.subject: IGF2BP2
relationships.evidence_quote: These data demonstrated the important role of IGF2BP2, an m6A reader, in the maintenance of Grin2a mRNA stability in DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: DBP
relationships.evidence_quote: These results show that DBP regulates the transcription of Mettl14 by binding to its promoter

relationships.subject: METTL14
relationships.evidence_quote: siMettl14 intrathecal injection notably attenuated paclitaxel-induced pain behaviors, including mechanical hypersensitivity

relationships.subject: TCN 201
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal injection of TCN 201, a specific antagonist of GluN2A-containing NMDARs (27), observably reversed mechanical allodynia, thermal hyperalgesia, and cold allodynia induced by METTL14 overexpression in naive rats

key_findings: Paclitaxel increases DRG METTL14 (via DBP) and m6A, which stabilizes Grin2a/GluN2A mRNA through the reader IGF2BP2
METTL14 knockdown attenuates CINP and presynaptic NMDAR hyperactivity; overexpression induces pain hypersensitivity
